112.1.rationale: Cards on the stack are spells, distinct from abilities. The legal-target enumeration defect has a regression and a shared fix. Full spell lifecycle and dependent copy rules remain to be assessed. Countering spells and distinguishing stack abilities are now exercised through shared selectors.
gaps: Copy spells and copy-card casting are unreviewed

400.7.rationale: Zone changes create new identities. Reanimation and linked-return tests cover stale references, including a physical card leaving and returning to the same zone. This does not establish every exception in the subrules. Explicit graveyard cost pools now share selection and validation; regressions cover exact payment, ownership, stale identities, cost references, target invalidation and mana planning from graveyards.
gaps: Review exceptions 400.7a through 400.7m individually

607.2a.rationale: Existing Angel of Serenity and Oblivion Ring tests exercise linked exile, owner destinations, mixed graveyard/battlefield targets, and the source leaving before exile resolves. Repeated activations and copying linked abilities need further review.
gaps: Linked-ability interaction with copy effects is unreviewed

800.4a.rationale: Departed players cannot act or be targets, including opponent/planeswalker unions. Owned-object removal and priority transfer are tested. Control-changing effects on departure remain unreviewed.
gaps: End control-changing effects before exiling remaining controlled objects
Stack copies controlled but not owned by a departing player

800.4d.rationale: Pending damage triggers are removed when their controller leaves before they reach the stack, while surviving players' triggers remain. The separate object-creation clause is not yet assessed.
gaps: Prevent creation of objects that would be owned by departed players

800.4j.rationale: Three- and four-player tests show that the active player's turn continues after their elimination, with priority passing to living players. Other elimination timing windows still need review.
gaps: Elimination during combat, cleanup and paused resolution

800.4k.rationale: The turn successor skips a departed player in a four-player game. Simultaneous losses now terminate correctly with either a winner or a draw. Extra-turn scheduling remains unsupported.
gaps: Extra-turn scheduling is unsupported

702.34a.rationale: Flashback tests establish graveyard permission, ownership, costs, timing, resolution, and exile when all targets become illegal. Unburial Rites supplies the reanimation interaction. The exile replacement now lives in the shared zone-change path; countering and returning a flashback spell to hand are tested.
gaps: Competing stack-departure replacement effects
Non-mana flashback costs

701.6a.rationale: Spells and activated/triggered abilities can be countered through typed card text. Tests cover destinations, no resolution, source independence, invalid targets, uncounterability and flashback; Counterspell and Dissolve have completed reference comparisons. Copy objects and counter-event triggers remain unreviewed.
gaps: Copy spells/abilities
Triggers that look back at counter events (603.10e)

701.6b.rationale: The counter action only removes its stack object. It does not touch mana or undo paid costs. The focused test verifies both spent mana and a sacrificed ability source remain spent; the ability creates no graveyard card. This rule has no separate textual form: counter grammar acceptance/rejection is covered by the 701.6a evidence.

113.6g.rationale: A shared static-ability classification applies own-object countering prohibitions on the stack, excluding them from resolution instructions. Tests cover permanent and sorcery spells, dynamic conditions, battlefield global protection and exile. Supreme Verdict agrees with XMage in a completed scenario.
gaps: The cannot-be-copied clause requires copy effects

104.4a.rationale: When every remaining player loses simultaneously, the game terminates without a winner. Direct tests cover two, three and four players, refusal of further actions, and the contrasting case with one survivor. The Flame Rift reference scenario completes as a draw. This rule has no special card-text form; other ways to draw are separate rules.

603.2.rationale: Each occurrence of damage, life gain or life loss preserves its actual quantity for triggered instructions referring to that much/many. Tests distinguish separate events from accumulated damage, retain quantities after source death and across paused/cloned choices, and reject an unbound quantity. This is only part of trigger detection and its subrules.
gaps: Other quantitative event kinds and quantity references to earlier instructions
Review all trigger detection exceptions and subrules

701.24a.rationale: Library shuffles preserve the card multiset, use cloned deterministic random state, hide faces and leave other libraries untouched. Face-down piles and other shuffle destinations are not implemented.
gaps: Face-down piles and shuffle-into-library instructions

701.24e.rationale: The common library shuffle method emits the shuffle event unconditionally. Zero- and one-card tests cause the watching ability to trigger and resolve against the correct player, despite unchanged order.

701.23a.rationale: A private search decision exposes the whole library to its searching owner and only matching cards can be selected. Shared card selectors, references, moves and entry effects execute the subsequent instructions. Pipe visibility and atomic invalid-answer rejection are tested.
gaps: Other players searching a library and searches of other zones
Search-event triggers

701.23b.rationale: A qualified search of ones own library may find no cards even when matching cards exist. An empty result replaces the previous antecedent. The fail-to-find reference scenario completes in agreement.
gaps: Other hidden zones and several described groups in one search

701.23d.rationale: Unqualified searches require the stated number, capped by the number of cards available. Tests cover empty, insufficient, exact and excess libraries and rejection of choosing too few.
gaps: Other hidden zones

701.23e.rationale: Found cards remain private unless an explicit reveal instruction executes. Tests distinguish the public reveal event from the private card now in hand.
gaps: Other searching players and zones

701.24b.rationale: Found cards are excluded from a shuffle immediately followed by their placement, including a position in that library. Placed cards and cards whose earlier optional move was declined participate in later shuffles. Complex intervening instructions are rejected until separate set-aside semantics are modeled.
gaps: Intervening instructions between shuffle and placement
Combined searches before a shuffle

701.20d.rationale: A revealed library card that participates in a shuffle becomes a new hidden object without changing zones. A later instruction cannot move the old object. Found cards held aside are not randomized. Reveal itself now checks the current objects against its action signature, so it cannot emit another reveal of the disappeared identity.
gaps: Reordering by operations other than shuffle
Continuously revealed top cards

100.1.rationale: The pipe requires at least two initial seats and the core runs N-player games. The low-level Game::new constructor itself does not enforce that precondition.
test_specs: Reject zero/one-seat public setup without mutation; retain two-, three- and four-player setup and continuation fixtures.

100.2.rationale: Decks, tokens, counters and life have explicit state representations. Format construction requirements and supplementary decks remain dependencies in its subrules.
test_specs: Check setup, token/counter representation and player observations; assess every deck-construction subrule separately.

100.2a.rationale: There is no format-aware constructed deck validator. Small hand-set boards and mechanism-test decks must remain available outside that validator.
test_specs: At the constructed-match boundary reject 59 cards and a fifth nonbasic English-name copy; accept 60 cards, unlimited basics and card-text exceptions. Count interchangeable names together (201.3).

100.2b.rationale: Limited card pools and format-specific deck validation are not represented.
test_specs: Reject a 39-card limited deck and cards absent from its pool; accept 40 cards and repeated pool copies beyond four, with permitted basic-land additions.

100.2c.rationale: Commander deck construction, commanders and color identity are not implemented. This remains in the initial delivery scope.
test_specs: Use the 903 audit to specify deck size, singleton exceptions, color identity and commander eligibility; reject invalid decks at the Commander match boundary.

100.2d.rationale: Supplementary decks for Attractions, Planechase and Archenemy are deferred, not excluded.
test_specs: After their variant rules are modeled, construct valid and invalid supplementary decks and verify separation from the main library.

100.3.rationale: Seeded randomization exists for shuffling. Coin flips, dice actions and variant-specific components remain absent.
test_specs: Specify deterministic clone/replay tests for coin and die actions, legal outcome ranges, rerolls and associated events when implementing those actions.

100.4.rationale: Deck files distinguish sideboard rows and generated acceptance reports include them. There is no match-level sideboarding operation or format policy.
test_specs: Between games exchange deck and sideboard cards while preserving pool membership; reject a change during a game. Keep sideboard cards out of the initial library.

100.4a.rationale: No constructed sideboard-size or combined-copy validator exists.
test_specs: Reject 16 sideboard cards and a fifth nonbasic copy split across main/side; accept 15, fewer, unlimited basic copies and applicable card-text exceptions.

100.4b.rationale: Limited pools and individual sideboards are not modeled.
test_specs: Partition a limited pool between deck and sideboard without loss, duplication or unowned additions.

100.4c.rationale: Two-Headed Giant limited pools and team sideboards are deferred.
test_specs: Partition a team pool into two decks plus one shared sideboard, preserving every card exactly once.

100.4d.rationale: Other multiplayer team limited pools and assigned individual sideboards are deferred.
test_specs: Assign every unused team-pool card to one player; permit that player to sideboard it and reject transfer to another player.

100.5.rationale: The core stores arbitrary deck lengths, but minimum size is not selected or validated by format. Commander has a separate size requirement.
test_specs: Accept a legal constructed deck above 60 without an arbitrary upper bound, reject one below its minimum, and exercise the separate Commander exact-size policy.

100.6.rationale: Tournament format legality is an application policy not currently modeled. The referenced Tournament Rules are a separate specification; this audit does not import their changing contents.
test_specs: At a future tournament entry boundary supply a versioned format/legality policy and test allowed, restricted and banned card decisions. Do not hard-code one format into Game::new.

100.6a.rationale: The scripts run individual games, not a match with scoring and between-game choices. The rule describes usual defaults rather than a universal match-length mandate.
test_specs: Test a configurable match controller with two-player first-to-two defaults, game draws, sideboarding, and a one-game multiplayer default.

100.7.rationale: The corpus policy explicitly excludes funny-set and digital-only expansion; unsupported rules remain rejected. This paragraph describes material beyond the rulebook, not a demand to invent those rules.
test_specs: Add focused corpus-filter fixtures for funny sets, acorn/playtest examples and eligible ordinary paper cards when the data-fetch path is next changed.

100.1a.rationale: Two-player classification uses the initial seat count, which is retained throughout the game. The opening and first-draw tests exercise its observable consequences.

100.1b.rationale: More than two initial seats is multiplayer. Player records are retained after departure, so it does not become a two-player game when players leave. Free-mulligan and four-player departure tests provide representation and behavior evidence; this does not establish all of section 8.

100.6b.rationale: Informational pointer to an external event locator. It imposes no game-state transition, grammar form or runtime invariant. The extractor preserves this paragraph and URL. No artificial engine test is added; the current evidence gate conservatively awards no verified credit to a row without executed evidence_tests.

110.4a.rationale: The permanent-type predicate lives in the shared IR vocabulary and serves card selection and battlefield-entry eligibility. Tests enumerate all six types, reject instants/sorceries including kindred instants, accept kindred enchantments and multiple permanent types, distinguish cards from battlefield permanents, and compose search and Sun Titan. Classification does not assert implemented battle or planeswalker behavior.

401.4.rationale: Owners choose the order of simultaneous library placements before any cards move. Three-player tests cover APNAP, invalid answers, independent owner choices and indistinguishable public logs; pipe tests separately check privacy. Broader replacement interactions remain unreviewed. Destination replacements now share retained placement preparation across effects, cost parts and state-based batches. Nissa's Chosen and a full Clone copying it choose their private bottom order before either departs, retaining independent cloned answers and canonical public event ordering.
gaps: Competing replacement effects changing which cards arrive together

401.7.rationale: The shared placement operation counts from the top and clamps an out-of-range position to the bottom. Tests cover empty, shorter, boundary and longer libraries, with top/bottom contrasts. This is a positional rule; destination replacements have separate evidence.

101.1.rationale: Card instructions use shared actions, effects and restriction hooks to override particular defaults. The model has no universal coverage of those hooks, and concession at any time is not exposed.
gaps: Concession during priority, setup and paused resolution
Unimplemented rule-changing mechanisms
test_specs: Concede without priority and during another player’s choice; remove the departing player immediately and continue or end the game as appropriate.

101.2.rationale: Shared restrictions prevent forbidden actions, including countering, while preserving legal targeting and subsequent instructions. Coverage is partial because many prohibitions and requirements remain unsupported. Tajuru Preserver is now a compiled static causal prohibition: a resolving spell or ability retains its controller, and shared sacrifice choice eligibility consults the live prohibition before collecting simultaneous choices.
gaps: Audit remaining prohibition hooks and overlapping permissions
Causal prohibitions currently support sacrifice and the spell-or-ability union qualified only by controller; spell-only, ability-only, source characteristics and other causal actions remain refused.

101.2a.rationale: Ability removal is not modeled, so its exception to prohibition precedence has no implementation evidence.
test_specs: Give and remove the same ability under opposing timestamps; verify the layer result rather than treating removal as an absolute prohibition.

101.3.rationale: Supported instructions do as much as possible. Countering an uncounterable target still permits later instructions, and unavailable optional costs follow their specified consequences. Unimplemented actions and replacement combinations prevent a full assessment.
test_specs: Extend impossible-part composition cases as each action and replacement mechanism is implemented.

101.4.rationale: Direct tests exercise APNAP choices before simultaneous sacrifices, discards and library placement in multiplayer. Nested choices and restart semantics still need a general audit.
gaps: Nested choices and APNAP restart (101.4d)

101.4a.rationale: Hidden discards are selected by object identity, and other players cannot distinguish which was chosen before the simultaneous action. Private library orders are also concealed.
gaps: Review additional hidden-zone choice mechanisms as they are implemented

101.4b.rationale: The pipe now exposes earlier public sacrifice choices to later choosers, including forced choices. Three-player clone/resume tests ensure declarations are rebuilt once per instruction. Hidden choices remain private. Other kinds of public choices need review. Entry choices now expose prior consent/typed answers and the affected card, including one-shot returns; replay and clone tests check observations are not duplicated.
gaps: Other simultaneous public-choice kinds

101.4c.rationale: Written instructions execute in order, but there is no general player-selected ordering mechanism for several simultaneous unspecified choices.
test_specs: Construct two simultaneous independent choices for one player and exercise either order; contrast a specified ordering that cannot be reversed.

101.4d.rationale: The current resolver replays a fixed instruction sequence; APNAP restart for newly generated earlier-player choices is not established.
test_specs: Make a later player’s choice create a choice for an earlier seat while other choices remain; verify restart from the earliest outstanding APNAP seat.

101.4e.rationale: Opening decisions use the starting player as the first seat. Existing mulligan tests establish two-player and multiplayer behavior; other pregame actions remain unimplemented.
gaps: Other pregame actions and explicitly varied starting seats

102.1.rationale: The active seat denotes whose turn it is, independently of priority or the current chooser. Tests pass priority between seats and check APNAP beginning from seat one in a three-player game. Departed active-player turns have separate section 800 evidence.

102.2.rationale: For either controller in a two-player game, target opponent offers only the other player and rejects self-targeting without mutation. The contrasting target player accepts either player, including self, and both instructions resolve against the chosen player. Player conditions distinguish existential opponents from each opponent and exclude the querying controller.
gaps: Teams and variant-specific opponent relationships remain unimplemented.

102.3.rationale: Team membership is not represented. Free-for-all treats every other living player as an opponent; multiplayer team formats remain in the long-term target.
test_specs: In a four-player two-team fixture distinguish self, teammate and two opponents in both selector enumeration and explicit targeting.

102.4.rationale: The your-team selector is not represented, including its you-only meaning outside team games.
test_specs: In two-player and free-for-all games, your team affects only its controller; add the contrasting teammate case when teams are modeled.

106.3.rationale: Fixed mana symbols can be multiplied by a current count for spells and activated abilities. Resolution and payment estimates use one evaluator. Plans with state-dependent counts are verified by execution, avoiding false upper bounds before costs. Real-text Archdruid and Stronghold tests compose counts with costs and static effects; the Archdruid reference scenario completes in agreement. Production events now record the source and actual symbols; a targeted mana-producing trigger verifies the ability source.
gaps: Variable color choices after costs
General mana-production triggers
Triggered mana abilities (605.1b)

103.1.rationale: Setup accepts an explicit starting seat and rotates declarations and turns from it. Match scoring and the prior loser/draw chooser policy are not implemented.
test_specs: Test clockwise order from every starting seat in three/four-player setup; at the future match boundary test previous loser selection and chooser retention after a draw.

103.1a.rationale: Shared team turns have no starting-team representation.
test_specs: Choose a starting team, then exercise team-based opening declarations and first turn.
Select the archenemy as starting player regardless of a normal starting-player choice.

103.1c.rationale: Power Play and pregame starting-player overrides are deferred.
test_specs: Apply the card override after ordinary starting-seat selection and preserve the resulting pregame ordering.

103.2d.rationale: Sticker sheets and their setup are deferred.
test_specs: For constructed choose three revealed sheets reproducibly at random; for limited permit up to three owned sheets and retain their public identities.
Move chosen conspiracy cards from the sideboard to the command zone while preserving the remaining sideboard.
Shuffle each supplementary deck independently, preserving its membership and keeping it separate from libraries.

103.4a.rationale: Two-Headed Giant shared life is not modeled.
test_specs: Start each team at 30 shared life, not two individual totals.
Apply positive and negative avatar starting-life modifiers to the ordinary total.
Use 25 life for two players and 30 for more players, retaining the format after departures.
Start the archenemy at 40 while the other players receive their appropriate totals.
Apply positive and negative starting-hand modifiers to opening draws and mulligan limits.
Collect declarations from the starting team then other teams; let one teammate mulligan after another has kept.
Permit starting-team players to choose their internal action order before proceeding to the next team.
Skip phenomena by moving each to the planar deck bottom until a plane becomes the initial face-up plane.
Skip only the starting Two-Headed Giant team’s first draw step.

103.2.rationale: Ordinary starting decks are loaded without sideboard rows. The ordered variant-specific setup operations are absent.
test_specs: Once variant setup exists, assert the 103.2a–e ordering rather than running independent initialization hooks in arbitrary order.

103.2a.rationale: The deck-list reader excludes sideboard rows from the starting library. Substitute-card representation is not modeled.
test_specs: Add a deck-list fixture proving SB rows are excluded and all main copies retained; later test substitute cards by represented identity.

103.2b.rationale: Companion eligibility, public designation and outside-the-game storage are not implemented.
test_specs: Allow at most one owned legal companion, reject an ineligible deck or second designation, and keep the designated card outside the game.

103.2c.rationale: Commander setup remains in the initial target but is not implemented.
test_specs: Place each designated commander face up in the command zone before shuffling the remaining starting deck.

103.3.rationale: Seeded setup shuffles preserve card membership and replay. An opponent shuffle/cut interface and supplementary decks are not modeled.
test_specs: Test setup clone/replay and independence across three/four libraries; review whether an explicit optional cut has any observable digital-game obligation.

103.4.rationale: Setup accepts a starting life value and ordinary fixtures use 20. Format-aware defaults and differing per-player/team starting totals are not modeled.
test_specs: Test a format setup boundary that selects ordinary and variant totals rather than requiring the caller to supply them.

103.4c.rationale: The generic constructor can receive 40, but no Commander setup policy exists.
test_specs: Starting a Commander game selects 40 life for every player without manual state edits.

103.5.rationale: Opening declarations, simultaneous redraw rounds, ordered bottoming, keeping and the zero-card mulligan limit have direct tests. Modified starting hands and nonstandard pregame actions remain absent.
test_specs: Add multiplayer rounds with different keep/mulligan histories, invalid bottom choices preserving state, clone/replay and opponent-view privacy.

103.5b.rationale: No alternate pregame action may be taken instead of a mulligan declaration.
test_specs: Allow a qualifying action before declaring in any round, including after other seats have declared, and still require that player’s declaration afterward.

103.5c.rationale: More than two initial seats receive a free first mulligan. Two-player Brawl is not distinguished from ordinary two-player games. Four-player mixed rounds also test independent histories, atomic invalid bottom choices, hidden-card visibility and clone/replay.
test_specs: When Brawl setup exists, test its free first mulligan even with only two players.

103.6.rationale: Setup begins the first turn immediately after mulligans, with no opening-hand action phase.
test_specs: Offer all eligible opening-hand actions to each player in APNAP order after mulligans, allowing their own action order, before beginning the first turn.

103.6a.rationale: Opening-hand battlefield placement is not implemented.
test_specs: Use a Leyline example to enter before the first turn, preserving ownership, entry effects and subsequent ordinary casting.

103.6b.rationale: Opening-hand reveal actions and their reveal duration are not implemented.
test_specs: Reveal an eligible card at most once, keep it visible through remaining pregame actions, and end its reveal when the first turn starts.

103.8.rationale: After opening choices finish, the explicitly selected starting player begins turn one. A nonzero starting seat is tested.

103.8a.rationale: The first player in an ordinary two-player game skips the first draw step; the next player draws normally. The direct test checks hand sizes and the phase transition.

103.8c.rationale: The first-draw skip applies only with two initial seats. Direct tests start three- and four-player games from every possible starting seat and verify each player draws on their first turn. This establishes the ordinary multiplayer draw rule, not the unimplemented variants as a whole.

106.12.rationale: A dedicated event distinguishes resolving mana abilities with tap-symbol costs from ordinary taps, untapped-sacrifice costs and tap abilities that use the stack. Direct tests cover those contrasts. Mana activation during another action’s payment remains absent.
gaps: Mana activation inside casting/other cost-payment transactions (605.3a)

106.12a.rationale: A tapped-for-mana event occurs once after a tap-cost mana ability resolves and actually produces mana. Zero production is excluded. Sacrificed sources use last-known characteristics without reviving departed watchers. A completed Burning Earth reference scenario agrees.
gaps: Triggers restricted to a specified mana type
Triggered mana abilities (605.1b)

605.1b.rationale: Admission distinguishes targetless mana-producing mana-event triggers from ordinary targeted triggers. The former are refused because immediate resolution is not modeled; the latter resolve on the stack and record the ability source as the mana source.
gaps: Immediate triggered-mana resolution and its recursive event timing

605.3a.rationale: Priority mana activation, casting-time plans and activation-time plans run without intermediate settlement. A mana ability can use another to pay its own cost. A nonmana cost does not grant a mana activation window. Explicit graveyard cost pools now share selection and validation; regressions cover exact payment, ownership, stale identities, cost references, target invalidation and mana planning from graveyards.
gaps: Mana payment requested during resolution
Interactive nested payment choices beyond complete ordered plans

702.11b.rationale: Ordinary permanent hexproof is declared by its rule sentence in the shared restriction system. Target enumeration, explicit choices, trigger viability and resolution consult that restriction with the spell/ability controller. It does not alter selector membership. Tests cover all three seats, own targets, abilities with sacrificed sources, gained and expired hexproof, all/partly illegal targets, and nontargeting sweeps. Thrun and response-time Ranger’s Guile scenarios agree with XMage. Player and quality-specific hexproof are separate subrules.

702.11c.rationale: Players do not have a general keyword-ability representation. Permanent hexproof support does not establish player hexproof.
test_specs: Grant a player hexproof; allow their own targeting spells/abilities and refuse opponents’ at announcement and resolution, while retaining nontargeting effects.

702.11d.rationale: Quality-specific hexproof and spell/source-quality target prohibitions remain rejected. The current target-prohibition hook knows the targeting controller, not a complete spell/ability source description.
test_specs: Add a targeting context that distinguishes spells from abilities and retains source characteristics/LKI; test matching and nonmatching source qualities and opponent versus own control.

702.18a.rationale: Permanent shroud uses the same sentence-based target-prohibition hook as hexproof. Tests reject even the controller’s targets, leave nontargeting sweeps and Aura entry attachments legal, and restrict keyword functioning to the battlefield. Player shroud is not implemented.
gaps: Player keyword abilities, including shroud

104.1.rationale: The engine ends ordinary elimination wins and simultaneous-loss draws and refuses subsequent actions. Explicit outcome effects and restarting are absent.
gaps: Win/loss/draw effects and restarted games

104.2.rationale: Last-survivor wins are modeled; other winning methods remain missing or deferred.

104.2a.rationale: The last surviving player wins in two-player and free-for-all games. Existing simultaneous-elimination tests exercise this result; team opponents and prevention-of-winning effects are not modeled.
test_specs: Confirm the last survivor wins immediately even when an effect prevents that player from winning by other means.

104.2b.rationale: No action currently declares a player the winner.
test_specs: Execute a win effect during resolution and stop remaining instructions immediately; test a prohibition on winning.

104.2c.rationale: Team identity and team outcomes are deferred.
test_specs: End with one surviving team and credit every member, including previously eliminated teammates.
An emperor winning immediately wins for that team regardless of surviving opponents.

104.3.rationale: Life and failed-draw losses are exercised; concession, poison, explicit loss effects and Commander damage remain missing.

104.3a.rationale: There is no concession action. It must work beyond priority, including pending choices, rather than being treated as an ordinary priority move.
test_specs: Concede during another player’s priority, a resolving choice, and opening setup; in multiplayer preserve surviving choices and continue the turn correctly.

104.3b.rationale: Zero and negative life cause loss at the next state-based-action check before priority. Direct tests cover recovery during a paused resolving effect, refusal to lose mid-resolution, ordinary ability costs, immediate mana ability recovery, and three-player continuation. Loss-prevention effects are a separate rule-changing mechanism.

104.3c.rationale: Draw processes available cards, records a failed draw independently of later library contents, and loses at the next priority check. Tests distinguish drawing zero from an empty library, a partly successful draw followed by refilling during a paused effect, and ordinary empty-library loss.

104.3d.rationale: Players have no poison-counter representation or poison loss check.
test_specs: At nine poison survive; at ten or more lose before priority, allowing removal during the same resolving effect and checking simultaneous losses.

104.3e.rationale: No effect action currently makes a player lose.
test_specs: An explicit loss instruction eliminates immediately during resolution, respecting loss prohibitions and multiplayer continuation.

104.3f.rationale: Simultaneous explicit win/loss outcomes cannot yet be represented.
test_specs: Resolve simultaneous win and loss for the same player and select loss; contrast effects that prevent only one outcome.
One teammate’s loss leaves the team alive; elimination of the last member loses for the team.

104.3h.rationale: Limited range of influence and explicit outcome effects are not modeled.
test_specs: A win effect eliminates only opponents within range and leaves distant surviving players in the game.
Losing an emperor eliminates that team while losing a general does not.

104.3j.rationale: Commander damage needs persistent commander identity and per-opponent combat-damage history. This remains in the first delivery target.
test_specs: Accumulate 20 then 21 combat damage from one commander across zone changes; do not combine different commanders or count noncombat damage, and do not erase history when life is gained.

104.3k.rationale: Tournament judge interventions are outside current engine interfaces.
test_specs: An administrative game-loss input should use the common elimination path and preserve its external reason.

104.4.rationale: Simultaneous elimination draws are modeled; mandatory-loop detection and explicit draw effects remain absent.

104.4b.rationale: A simulation step limit is not a rules draw, and the engine has no mandatory-loop adjudication.
test_specs: Contrast a forced recurring state with a loop having an optional exit; declare only the mandatory loop a draw and retain the repeated-state witness.

104.4c.rationale: No effect action currently declares a draw.
test_specs: End immediately when a draw effect resolves and execute no later instruction.
When every remaining team loses simultaneously, end in a draw rather than select a last processed team.

104.4e.rationale: Limited range of influence and per-player draw outcomes are absent.
test_specs: A draw effect removes its controller and players within range while the distant players continue.
Compute the participants and their influence ranges for a mandatory loop; remove only affected players and continue for the rest.
Draw for a team only when all its remaining members have drawn.
Drawing for an emperor draws for the team, unlike a general’s individual draw.

104.4i.rationale: Tournament draw agreements are outside current engine interfaces.
test_specs: Require agreement from all participants and terminate with an intentional-draw reason.

104.5.rationale: Losses remove players and their owned objects, transfer priority and suppress pending triggers. Individual draw outcomes and some control-changing departure rules remain absent.
gaps: Per-player draw outcomes
Control-changing effects and pending choices on departure

104.6.rationale: Restarting the game is explicitly deferred; it is not ordinary setup after declaring a winner.
test_specs: Restart with only players still participating, apply Karn’s set-aside exceptions, and discard prior turn, priority and effect state.

118.3.rationale: Atomic transactions reject incomplete payments without mutating the original state.
gaps: Planner does not find all costs made affordable by life gain, untapping or fresh identities during mana activation

118.10.rationale: Joint object-payment selection and validation prevent reusing one object for multiple payments. Plural object payments are one event; separate cost parts capture triggers before later parts remove their sources.
gaps: General cost replacements and freely chosen payment ordering remain unsupported

400.7j.rationale: Mandatory fixed additional spell costs share activated payment validation and transactional execution. Costs are paid before resolution, combine with flashback, retain plural public-zone references and last-known information, and do not change mana value. Focused multiplayer tests and completed Village Rites/Bone Splinters comparisons provide scoped evidence.
gaps: Participial references such as Fling remain refused; broader references need review

601.2h.rationale: Mandatory fixed additional spell costs share activated payment validation and transactional execution. Costs are paid before resolution, combine with flashback, retain plural public-zone references and last-known information, and do not change mana value. Focused multiplayer tests and completed Village Rites/Bone Splinters comparisons provide scoped evidence. A retained commitment advances through each cost part once. Library ordering may pause a sacrifice after earlier mana/life or object parts have committed; the next part evaluates its replacements against the resulting state.
gaps: Optional and variable additional costs remain refused
Arbitrary legal payment ordering and replacement interactions remain incomplete

301.5.rationale: Ordinary Equipment attach only to creatures through shared attachment legality. Subrules retain gaps for entry-attached effects, reconfigure and control-changing effects.

614.5.rationale: Each applicable multiplier is applied once, including separate instances on one permanent, without recursively reapplying the effect to its own result. 614.6.rationale: Only the modified life-gain event occurs and triggers Pridemate once; zero and prohibited gains create no event. gaps: General substituted multi-action events and impossible replacement instructions remain unimplemented.
